title: Event
description:
One thing the panel is told.

Tagged by its name in snake_case beside its fields, as a task and a
query are: `{"type": "changed", "scopes": [...]}`.

oneOf.description:
Something a backend watches changed on disk, so what the panel shows
of each scope may be out of date: one event for every change the
watcher took in together, each scope once, in the backend's words.
A task's lines started to run on the writer thread.
They stopped, however that went: the reply to the run says how.

How far the run of these lines has got, as its backend says it
([`Running::report`](crate::Running::report)): told between its
start and its finish, each time the backend says something new, and
never for a run whose backend says nothing, which is most of them.

A run of these lines is under way, and `waiting` jobs, runs and
switches, wait their turn behind it on the writer thread: told as
each is sent while it runs, and as a run starts with some still
behind it, so a panel says why what it sent has not started.

The backend acts on something else since ([`Backend::switch`]),
and what it names is watched: everything is to be asked for again,
and nothing shown before kept, since it was of what it acted on
before. Told on the writer thread, once the switch is taken, to
every subscriber, the tab that asked for it among them
([`Events::switched`]), with how many switches were taken since the
bus was made, this one counted.

[`Backend::switch`]: crate::Backend::switch

The subscriber may have missed something: it has just connected, or
it fell behind. Everything is to be asked for again.

With how many switches were taken since the bus was made, as the
latest [`Switched`](Event::Switched) said: a subscriber that missed
one, a tab whose stream was let go while it was hidden or one that
fell behind, learns it from a count other than the one it heard last,
and lets go of what it shows of what the backend acted on before as
it would on hearing `Switched`. A count rather than a word that a
switch happened, which only a bus that knew what each subscriber had
heard could say.

Every path the backend named is watched, so a change to one arrives
as [`Changed`](Event::Changed).

Not every one is, so a change there arrives as nothing, and what the
panel shows is refreshed by hand: the system's limit on watches was
reached, or a watch could not be set up at all.

Progress.description:
How far a run under way has got, as its backend says it
([`Running::report`]): what a `progress` event carries
([`Event::Progress`](crate::Event::Progress)).

The server's own shape, with the backend's words in it: a step, how many
of it are done and of how many, and whether a cancel still stops the
run. What the steps are, and from which one a cancel comes too late,
are the front end's rules, a gather's, so the backend says both, and
the server carries them unread, as it carries a scope. JSON of the
backend's own in its place was the other way, and is rejected: a panel
draws a count the same whatever counts it, and the description of the
API then says what an event holds, for a script to read by it.

cancellable.description: Whether a cancel sent now still stops the run.

done.description: How many of the step are done.

message.description: The same, for a person, with its counts: `receiving objects 12/40`.

step.description:
What the run is doing, as one word of the backend's own, in
snake_case: `receiving`.

total.description: Of how many, once that is known.
